correctness.rationale: For m plants and r pollinators, each plant has a nonempty r-bit neighbor mask, and protecting j gives exact Bernstein-basis survival coefficients c_j(k) counting k-subsets of r−1 remaining pollinators that cover all m plants. Permuting plant rows permits exhaustive enumeration of all nondecreasing masks, with labelled pollinators preserved. An independently written exhaustive connected bipartite graph enumerator checked precisely 64,820 row-multiset representatives for 2≤m,r and m+r≤9, and independently calculated every c_j(k): a coefficientwise global dominator exists in every case; the one-guild-singleton cases follow directly. Positive basis weights imply a common probability maximizer for all p∈(0,1). For ten-species plant masks (3,5,14,22,26), independent enumeration gives A=(0,1,6,4,1), B=(0,2,5,4,1), C=(0,1,5,4,1), D=E=(0,0,4,4,1); B−A=p(1−p)²(1−2p) so B uniquely wins below 1/2, A uniquely above, and only A,B tie at 1/2. This is a finite exhaustive theorem plus an exact polynomial witness, not extrapolation to larger networks.

originality.rationale: QUALIFIED PASS. Classical coherent-system component-importance ranking by minimal cuts (Butler 1977) and ecological network robustness/nestedness (Bascompte et al 2003; Kaiser-Bunbury et al 2010) address the underlying type of incidence reliability, but do not in inspected material establish the *minimum total bipartite vertex count* for a change of best perfectly protected component under the all-plants retained event. A later reliability survey concerns all-terminal structural reliability, not this choice of perfectly guaranteed pollinator. Equivalence under monotone Boolean CNF/stochastic set cover remains a real priority risk, especially with the 1977 full paper unavailable.
